title: Bizarre acts connected to heroin cut with caffeine
article: A drug found in the possession of a crazed man clinging to the front of a B.C. Transit Bus last week has been identified as heroin cut with caffeine.
Police are waiting for further analysis of the drug by toxicologists at the Health Protection Branch lab in Burnaby, said Victoria police Staff Sgt. Peter Lawson.

The man, who was partially clothed and screaming, was restrained and taken to hospital last Thursday morning. He was the third person in the area exhibiting paranoid and violent behaviour when picked up by police.

On Aug. 21, Mladen Cujko, a 33-year-old known drug user from Burnaby, died during a struggle with a Western Communities RCMP officer on the Trans-Canada Highway. Cujko had been screaming for help, running in and out of traffic on Jacklin Road.
Drugs, hidden in a Baggy in his underwear, had been identified as cocaine cut with caffeine. However, police can't be sure he had taken those drugs.
A toxicology report also indicated it would be "unusual" for cocaine cut with caffeine to produce such a violent response in an individual.
Vancouver Island RCMP major crimes officers are continuing to investigate Cujko's death.
According to Lawson, the police forces are comparing notes and co- ordinating analysis of drug samples taken from at least four people exhibiting violent, paranoid behaviour.
